subject: MAP runup: POC activation roadmap — org seed, API keys, IP safelist & VPC peering

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health DevOps <devops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: MAP runup: POC activation roadmap — org seed, API keys, IP safelist & VPC peering

Hi Sarah + DevOps team,

Great to have you onboard for the POC. Per our success criteria call, I put together a short runup to lock the MAP items we'll need to activate the environment. Goal: get a functional evaluation environment (hosted/dedicated hybrid) within 7 business days of gating items being complete.

High-level asks (what we need from Acme):
- Org seed: create an org account for the POC and add stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai and karthik_iyer@redwood.ai as Org Admins. This lets us provision scoped API keys.
- API keys: once org exists, we'll hand off a scoped read/write key for the trial. We prefer short-lived keys for the POC; we can exchange via DocuSign/secure vault.
- IP safelist: list of outbound IPs that will call your services (we will provide Redwood egress ranges). Please also provide the IP ranges you will allow inbound for webhook callbacks.
- VPC peering: optional but recommended for the dedicated nodes. If you want peering, please review the attached peering template and confirm your VPC ID, CIDR, and preferred peering window.

Proposed timeline (draft MAP):
1) Day 0 (today): Org created + initial contact person assigned (Sarah?)
2) Day 1–2: Exchange API key provisioning method + share IP safelist requirements
3) Day 3–5: Test inbound/outbound connectivity, exchange ephemeral key, smoke test generation & embeddings
4) Day 6–7: Optional VPC peering window (coordinate maintenance window) + final acceptance signoff for POC metrics

I've attached a short runup PDF with the MAP items and a VPC peering template (acme-vpc-peering-template.txt). Please confirm owners and any blackout windows. If you'd rather have Engineering run the peering prep, loop in a ticket or paste the VPC details to reply.

Next steps from our side: Karthik will prepare the short-lived API key flow and a quick checklist for the IP ranges we need to be safelisted. Neha will own peering coordination if you choose that option.

Thanks — excited to get you spun up.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-map-runup-v1.pdf (pdf)]

Stephanie, thanks — this is helpful.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Org owner: I'll ask IT to spin up the org and add your two folks as admins by EOD tomorrow.
- API key exchange: we need the scoped key details (scopes + TTL) to route through our secrets rotation process. Can you provide the TTL and scopes you recommend?
- IP safelist: we'll need the specific egress ranges from Redwood to put on our firewall. Also we'll share our webhook receiver IPs.
- VPC peering: we prefer peering during our change window on Friday night (UTC). We'll confirm the CIDR tomorrow.

Can Karthik include the minimal recommended scopes and TTL in one email so we can build the ticket? Also, please send the egress ranges (or a short list) that the POC will use.

Regards,
Sarah Lin
Head of Integrations, Acme Health

Hi all — quick tech note to make the handoff smoother. Below are the minimal items and example values Acme can paste into their ticketing system.

1) API key scopes & TTL (recommended)\- Scopes: generation:read, generation:write, embeddings:read\- TTL: 8 hours (short-lived for POC); if you need longer, we can provision 7-day stacked keys with rotation hooks.

2) Redwood egress IP ranges (POC cluster) — please allow these outbound ranges for webhook + API calls:
- 34.210.12.0/24
- 35.199.44.0/24
- 52.204.128.0/24
(We will confirm the final list in the prod handoff doc; these are the POC set)

3) Inbound webhook receiver IPs — please confirm the endpoint and we'll provide a signature header to validate callbacks.

4) VPC peering template notes (from attached file):
- Your VPC ID: <REPLACE_WITH_VPC_ID>
- Your CIDR: <REPLACE_WITH_VPC_CIDR>
- Required routes: add a route for Redwood CIDR 172.31.0.0/16 to the peering connection
- Security groups: allow TCP 443 between subnets used by the POC nodes

5) Test checklist (smoke tests):
- API key: token grant and short token refresh
- Generation: 1x 1kB completion request, measure latency < 500ms median
- Embeddings: 10 item batch embed, verify vector size and format

If you want, I can paste this into a short Confluence article or the HubSpot ticket for your IT. Neha will coordinate peering times.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick responses — appreciate it. Confirming the MAP items and owners below so we can close the gating checklist: 

Owners and commitments:
- Org creation (owner: Sarah / Acme IT): Org created and both Redwood admins added by 2026-06-23 EOD (pending)
- API key provisioning (owner: Acme IT + Karthik): implement short-lived TTL and provide ticket for secret rotation by 2026-06-24
- IP safelist (owner: Acme DevOps): add Redwood egress ranges listed by Karthik to firewall rules by 2026-06-24
- VPC peering (owner: Neha + Acme DevOps): target peering window Friday 2026-06-25 22:00 UTC (confirm if this works for you)

Acceptance criteria for POC go/no-go:
- Successful token issuance and one successful generation request from POC cluster within 24 hours of keys being provisioned
- Webhook callbacks reach the Acme receiver and validate signature header
- (Optional) Peered connectivity verified at the network layer; otherwise we will proceed over the public egress routes for the POC

Please reply with any edits. If this looks good, I'll update the HubSpot deal with the MAP items and timeline and we can move to the ticketing exchange.

Best,
Stephanie
